plan.rationale: The torch collector already ran and coverage.json shows complete attribution (66441/66441 kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 ambiguous forward sequences), so no overlap, graph-tracing or attribution question remains for nsys to resolve, and it is not selected. The frozen objective is ttft_ms for a single-GPU BF16 SDPA Qwen3-4B prefill (batch 1, 256 prompt tokens) whose timed boundary is wall-clock perf_counter_ns around model() plus an explicit cuda.synchronize; observations.json marks communication not_applicable, so collective_calibration (a synthetic full-world SUM allreduce reference experiment, not a performance lower bound or critical-path estimate) is excluded as it cannot inform a single-device inference objective, and candidate_diagnostics is excluded because no candidate set exists in the inputs. The open diagnostic questions for minimizing ttft_ms are: (1) how the measured first-token wall time splits between CPU submission/dispatch and GPU execution intervals, addressed by execution_timeline's CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization events, per-device intervals and clock alignment bounds (used only as diagnostics, never as a communication hook or to drive subsequent search actions, and its optional gradient post-accumulate callbacks stay off since there is no training); (2) which host-side Python dispatch and binding costs inflate the prefill submit stream, addressed by python_runtime's warmed cProfile call trace, accepted as perturbing and non-scoring; (3) coarse corroboration of GPU occupancy and memory footprint plus confirmation that PCIe traffic is negligible for GPU-resident inputs, addressed by device_telemetry's NVML utilization, memory and PCIe rate samples understood as device-wide readings with native windows, never per-collective or per-kernel bytes. Unavailable dimensions and the observed reasons for each are listed in unavailable_fields.
